title: The eight-piece brass band, Chicago and the Tennessee photo
summary: They count the instruments in the small brass band and look at later pictures from Chicago and Tennessee where he was bandmaster.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, yes. That's the small brass band. That's the old generation. And he's down here on the kneeling almost, or sitting on the ground, I guess. Sitting on the ground. This is it. With a big bass drum with a rope. And the snare drum. And right behind Mr. Matoya is a tuba. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Only an eight-piece band. I guess two carnets and tuba and trombone. Two drums, alto horn. Oh, that's a baritone there. There. There's the tuba. That's all they had.
And how many do they have in this one?
This is a regular brass band. Eight. Four, five, six. Only eight pieces. I've heard of the old.
They have the baritone.
And the alto horn.
And the upright bass.
Yeah, there's the bass.
Upright bass and baritone. And the alto horn. This is the alto horn. They call it French horn.
No clarinets, I believe.
I don't see them. Two carnets.
Two drummers, of course. Two carnets.
And this is the one the National Soldiers Field in Chicago. That's a late one.
Oh, yes.
Where is it? I want to. No, not that. That's Chicago.
Which is Mr. Matoye. I don't see.
No, right. Right here. He's holding his arm. See him right there? Right there?
Yes.
No, right here.
Oh, yes. On the first, next to the drummer. You recognize him? Sure, I see now.
Yeah, that's right.
Next to the snare drummer.

On the front row. And you remember when I told you about Mama, him going off and going to Tennessee? Oh, yes. This is the last picture of him. It's the last picture. Just before I left. That's the one in Tennessee. They say he was bandmaster.
With the flag there and all. Mm-hmm. Must have been on a big stage, I guess, over here.
Yeah, it was a big stage.
And his picture is up in the little round picture up in the corner of that.
